notes: Strong baseline — eval 2 assertions test output quality which both agents achieved. Key difference is with_skill asked questions, without_skill didn't — but assertions don't capture that for this eval.
The most decisive difference is eval 0: with_skill asked 5 questions before designing, without_skill asked 0. This is the core behavior change from the new SKILL.md intake step.
Eval 1 shows the requirement acknowledgment behavior: with_skill formally listed all requirements before proceeding, without_skill did not.

Eval 2 is a tie on assertions — both agents independently converged on a split-panel layout and named the same AI patterns. The with_skill edge (asking questions first) isn't captured by eval 2's current assertions. Consider adding an assertion for this.
The skill costs ~2x tokens and ~2x time. Expected tradeoff for a skill that reads reference files and does more deliberate planning.

Palette specificity (eval 0 assertion 3) failed for both agents — with_skill used #3B5BDB, without_skill used #4F46E5. Both are blue/indigo family. The SKILL.md's anti-generic section needs to more actively push color specificity, not just layout specificity.
